Sutures out = fully healed? Not quite.

It’s easy to think that once the visible sutures have been removed, the incision is healed and there’s nothing left holding everything together. But healing continues beneath the surface. For many procedures, deeper dissolvable sutures remain underneath the skin, supporting the tissues while the body continues to heal. Over time, these sutures are gradually broken down and absorbed by the body.

The incision itself is also still developing strength, while the scar continues to settle, soften and mature over the weeks and months that follow. Suture removal is an important milestone, but it’s just one stage of the recovery process.

A great facelift lifts tissue. It doesn’t replace lost fat. That’s why so many results still look hollow.

There are two forces of aging: 1.) Gravity, and 2.) Atrophy (loss of good fat). Today, getting a great lift to overcome gravity is necessary but not sufficient. The lost volume must be replaced in kind, and so often it's not.

All too often I see results that are over-resected. Hollow, skeletal, beady. 

For my wonderful patient, I performed top-down fat transfer. Micro-fat in the tear troughs, cheeks, deep lines, lateral lips, pre-jowl sulcus and chin. Nano-fat in the fine lines, particularly around the eyes and mouth. 

The result is elegant, full and rejuvenated.

Altogether she had:
*  Extended Deep Plane Facelift
*  Deep Neck Lift
*  Endoscopic Brow Lift
*  Custom Fat Transer (nano and micro)
*  Lip Lift

She is four months out and is genuinely beautiful inside and out.

Anita@oklandfacialplasticsurgery.com

One week after Deep Plane Facelift, Deep Neck Lift, Endoscopic Brow Lift ⭐️

Kristen is glowing. The first day or two she described as "a little rough", but by one week she feels comfortable being out in public with her hair down to cover her incisions. 

NOTE - Kristen's healing is above average for this stage of recovery. Most patients are 2-3 weeks until they feel comfortable at a casual dinner or grocery store without noticeable evidence of surgery. 

Pain - Kristen described feeling relatively little pain. She took pain medication for the first 48 hours, and just Tylenol since then. She felt a headache for the first 48 hours from the brow lift. 

Tightness - she feels tightness in her neck and lower face, but not pain. 

Bruising - she has a small (quarter sized) bruise on her right lower neck, and a small bruise under her right eye - both of which are easily concealable with makeup. 

Energy - Kristen feels her energy level is almost back to normal. Still a little fatigued as the day goes on. She has been doing Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy sessions and feels they have been quite helpful in her recovery. 

⭐️ Keep following Kristen's journey. 🎥

I just wanted to be rid of the wrinkling on my neck and the jowels that were starting to form. People thought I was nuts because it was so subtle. But not to me! 
It was a no-brainer – gravity had taken its toll, I was also exhausted and I needed a “pick me up”. I entrusted my face to the best @drjacono and he hit it out of the park. 
He uses a method called deep plane which goes under the muscle so your skin is still attached. Your blood flows and your face stays vibrant and heals fast. 
Pick up his book #parkavenueface to read more. I did!
